title: feat(types): declare the handler key the `tree-view` renderer reads (objectui#7804 TreeViewSchema slice)
body:
Part of #7804 — slice 4 of the handler-key burn-down: the `TreeViewSchema` arm.

⛔ No closing keyword, deliberately: this card's ledger is not empty. Measured on this branch,

```
$ node -e 'import("./scripts/check-handler-key-read-sites.mjs").then(m=>{
    const k=[...m.KNOWN_UNDECLARED_READS.keys()];
    console.log("total",k.length,
                "| tree-view::",k.filter(x=>x.startsWith("tree-view::")).length,
                "| control list::",k.filter(x=>x.startsWith("list::")).length,
                "| control detail::",k.filter(x=>x.startsWith("detail::")).length);})'
total 14 | tree-view:: 0 | control list:: 5 | control detail:: 1
```

`KNOWN_UNDECLARED_READS` read **15** rows at this branch's base (`0b7be13`) and reads **14** here. `tree-view::` drained to **0**; the lit controls in the same pass are the five `list::` rows and the one `detail::` row, which are still there — so the zero is a reading, not an empty query.

## ⭐ The reading that should change how the rest of this card is sliced

The dispatch asked for the remaining-rows figure to be re-derived rather than quoted. The **count** held — 15 rows, and the release note's `form:: 4 · grid:: 1 · list:: 5` breakdown is still right. What did **not** hold is the sentence beside it: *"slice 4 answers objectui#9573 first, or picks from the **5** rows that are not that shape."*

Re-derived at this head from the **registration options** rather than from the type string, **13 of the 15 rows are the objectui#9573 alias shape**, not 10. A registration carrying `skipFallback: true` never claims the bare type key, while this census keys a registration by its RAW TYPE STRING — so the read is judged against an arm minted for a different component. Three rows nobody had scored that way are:

| row | registration measured on this tree | the arm it is judged against |
|---|---|---|
| `button::ButtonSchema.onSuccess` | `register('button', ActionButtonRenderer, { namespace: 'action', skipFallback: true })` | `form.zod.ts#ButtonSchema`, the Shadcn primitive registered by `renderers/form/button.tsx` |
| `icon::IconSchema.onSuccess` | `register('icon', ActionIconRenderer, { namespace: 'action', skipFallback: true })` | `layout.zod.ts#IconSchema` |
| `tabs::TabsSchema.onTabChange` | `register('tabs', PageTabsRenderer, { namespace: 'page', skipFallback: true })` | `layout.zod.ts#TabsSchema`, the `ui:tabs` arm from `renderers/layout/tabs.tsx` |

⇒ declaring `onSuccess` on `ButtonSchema` would publish an action's post-success navigation block on a plain button, exactly the way declaring the five `list::` keys would publish a density handler on a bullet list. ⛔ None of the three is drainable as written.

⭐ One of the three ANSWERS an open question rather than opening one: objectui#9344 ruled that its `tabs` row *"may be an ALIAS question rather than a declaration one"* and must not be co-disposed with `detail` until measured. It is measured here, and it is an alias question — but the alias is the **registration's**, not the `onValueChange` / `onTabChange` spelling's.

⇒ **the remainder after this PR is 14 rows: 13 alias-shape, plus `detail::DetailSchema.onTabChange`**, which is neither alias-shape nor drained and whose disposition is objectui#9344's item ②. That is the only row a slice 5 can take without answering objectui#9573 first. The finding is recorded in the ledger's own docblock, where the next slice reads it.

## What this slice does

`BaseSchema` is `.passthrough()`, so a key no arm declares is **not refused** — it stops being judged and the value is KEPT, then reaches the renderer that reads it. `TreeViewSchema.onNodeClick` sat in exactly that state while the registered `tree-view` renderer gated on `if (schema.onNodeClick)` and CALLED `schema.onNodeClick(node)`, so an authored `{ "type": "tree-view", "onNodeClick": { "action": "toast" } }` parsed GREEN and that object reached a call site expecting a function.

It is now `handlerKeyRefusal('onNodeClick', 'runtime-slot', 'Node click handler')` on `data-display.zod.ts#TreeViewSchema`, beside the two `'retired'` arms (`onSelectChange`, `onExpandChange`) the same schema already carried.

⚠️ **This row is NOT alias-shape, and that is the reason it was pickable.** `ComponentRegistry.register('tree-view', ..., { namespace: 'ui' })` carries no `skipFallback`, so the bare `tree-view` key is this component's own and this arm really is the contract for what renders under it. The fact is pinned off disk in the new test, not asserted in prose.

## The disposition, measured at this key's own channel

`'retired'` publishes *"no renderer reads this key, so nothing could ever run it"*. That is true of the two siblings already tombstoned on this arm and **flatly false** here, so the burden was on `'runtime-slot'`:

- **READ AND RUN** — the presence gate and the call are both in the `tree-view` registration's own `handleNodeClick`, and `node` is the clicked `TreeNode`.
- **The TypeScript face already declares the callable twin** (`data-display.ts#TreeViewSchema.onNodeClick`), so a function really does reach the renderer through the programmatic channel. This arm says on the JSON face what that face never could.
- ⚠️ **No in-repo supplier.** Nothing in `apps/`, `examples/` or `content/` builds a `tree-view` node carrying the key. That is the same shape as `ObjectFormSchema.onStepChange` in this card's `objectql.ts` slice — channel wired end to end, supplier absent — and it is ⛔ not evidence of a dead read. Reported rather than forced into the nearer box.

⚠️ **The `list-view` slice's precedence-type hazard does NOT apply here, and that is a reading rather than an omission.** `data-display.ts#TreeViewSchema` is a hand-written `interface ... extends BaseSchema`, not `z.input` of this mirror, so a refusal arm cannot AND the callable twin down to `undefined`. The new test carries the type-level pin that fails if the face is ever rebased onto the mirror — which is the only thing that would make this slice need a `ListViewAuthored` of its own.

## Evidence — two opposite reds out of one gate

**Directions predicted in writing before running. Both predictions held.**

**P1 — the INTERMEDIATE reading (arm declared, ledger row NOT yet removed).** Predicted RED on `staleExemptions()`. Measured `EXIT=1`, naming exactly the one row:

```
x  1 KNOWN_UNDECLARED_READS row(s) name a read site this gate no longer finds:
      tree-view::TreeViewSchema.onNodeClick
The defect the row waives is gone, so the row is now a live waiver for nothing. Delete it.
```

That is the proof the arm edit reached this exact key.

**P2 — ABLATION (arm reverted, ledger left drained).** Predicted RED the OTHER way. Measured `EXIT=1`:

```
x  1 handler key(s) a registered renderer reads are not declared by their arm:
      'tree-view'.onNodeClick  read at packages/components/src/renderers/data-display/tree-view.tsx:98
          registered in ...tree-view.tsx; TreeViewSchema (data-display.zod.ts) does not declare it.
```

- **Mutation proven on disk**, not by an exit code: the `onNodeClick: handlerKeyRefusal` anchor count went `1 -> 0` AND the on-disk blob hash moved off the HEAD blob (`9996fc9a...` to `fb169841...`).
- **Restore proven by state**: blob hash back to `9996fc9a...`, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- The whole leg ran from the COMMITTED state under `trap restore EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths, restoring with `git checkout HEAD -- path` (never the bare form, which takes the mutation back out of the index), and empty hashes were treated as FAILURE rather than as "nothing to compare".
- **No build step is involved**: this gate parses `packages/types/src/zod/*.zod.ts` from SOURCE through the TypeScript AST, and the suites resolve the mirror through a relative in-package specifier — there is no `dist/` layer that could keep a mutation alive or hide one.

**After the drain** the gate is green and prints its own count:

```
OK  105 arm(s), 212 registration(s) (119 with an arm), 60 reachable handler read(s),
    60 judged, 0 left unjudged ..., 14 exempted by ledger
```

## Authored-document census, with lit controls

This narrows a published accept set, so the zero had to be a reading and not a silence.

| corpus | files | `onNodeClick` | lit controls on the SAME corpus, same pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| all tracked `.json` / `.md` / `.mdx` / `.yml` / `.yaml` | 2630 | **0** | `"nodes"` 8 files · `"tree-view"` 9 files |
| tracked `apps/` + `examples/` TypeScript sources | 275 | **0** | `tree-view` 4 files · `nodes` 31 files |

A dark control in the same pass: `"onSelectChange"` also reads 0, which is what a key that is ALREADY a declared refusal should read. Every textual hit on `onNodeClick` anywhere in the tree is prose, a pin, or the renderer's own React prop — nothing authors it as metadata. Per this repository's fixed-version-group rule a `major` is not available, so the changeset declares `minor` with the narrowing spelled out.

## Ledger moves — all derived, none carried in from a card

| ledger | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `KNOWN_UNDECLARED_READS` | 15 rows | **14** |
| `handler-keys-json-refusal-6124.test.ts` `RUNTIME_SLOT` | 60 | **61** (site total 81 to 82) |
| `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` `KnownDrift` | 45 entries / 83 keys | **46 / 84** — a NEW entry, that pair had none |
| `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` | 4 entries / 10 keys | **3 / 9** — a whole ENTRY gone |

## ⚠️ The one structural consequence, stated because a digit does not carry it

`data-display.zod.ts#TreeViewSchema` was the ONE pair in `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` that was not also in `UnmirroredDeclared` — the entire content of the difference between them. Draining it makes `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` a **subset** of `UnmirroredDeclared` and the union equal to it exactly.

⇒ the header sentence that read `3 of the 4 ... the union is 15 pairs and not 14` now states the containment, and **two pin legs changed shape with it**: the union figure is read as one number instead of two, and the non-vacuity control that asserted `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` is NOT a subset now asserts that it IS, with the two non-vacuity legs it relied on (ledger non-empty, intersection non-empty) kept explicit. ⛔ That old leg is not a guard that got weakened — it is a claim about the ledgers that stopped holding, and keeping it would have forced a real key back onto a ledger to satisfy a sentence, which is the route this file exists to refuse.

## Gates run locally

| gate | verdict |
|---|---|
| `check:handler-key-reads` | exit 0 (green after the drain; red in BOTH ablation legs, as designed) |
| `packages/types/` suite, from the repo root | exit 0 — `Test Files 196 passed`, `Tests 4623 passed` |
| `@object-ui/types` `type-check` (3 tsconfigs) | `VERDICT command-exit 0`, under the shared verify lock |
| `scripts/__tests__/check-handler-key-read-sites.test.ts` | exit 0 — 30 tests |
| the ledger's other consumers (`plugin-detail`, `plugin-kanban`, `check-component-surface-parity`) | exit 0 — 69 tests |
| non-types suites that build a `tree-view` node (app-shell, cli, components x2) | exit 0 — 292 tests |
| `changeset:check` (fixed + no-major) · `check:changeset-claims` | exit 0 / exit 0 |
| `check:control-bytes` | exit 0 — 7770 tracked text files scanned |
| `check:new-line-citations` | exit 0, **0** new citations (two were added, then rewritten as content citations on the gate's own advice) |
| `check:test-path-roots` · `check:component-surface-parity` · `check:doc-types` · `check:registry-bare-names` · `check:spec-symbols` | exit 0 |
| `@object-ui/types` `lint` | exit 0 — 0 errors, 288 pre-existing warnings |

**Narrowing declared.** `pnpm lint` is `turbo run lint`, and CI owns the full farm; what ran here is the whole `@object-ui/types` package lint, which is not a narrowing of that package at all. `scripts/check-handler-key-read-sites.mjs` is outside every package `lint` target because `scripts/` has no `package.json` for turbo to walk — a fact about the repo, not a narrowing by this branch. Type-aware linting is not enabled (`eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it did not touch.

## Acceptance notes

Out-of-scope observations, noted and NOT filed:

- The `handler-keys-json-refusal-6124.test.ts` header prose still carries a `36 sites` figure that its own neighbouring sentence tells the reader not to quote, deferring to the length pin. Untouched — the file already says so about itself.
- `content/docs/components/data-display/tree-view.mdx` documents `onNodeClick` as a TypeScript member and says nothing about the JSON face. That matches every other runtime slot in the repo (`ButtonSchema.onClick` is documented the same way and has carried a refusal arm since objectui#6124), so it is a convention, not a defect this slice created. Successor if it is ever revisited: whoever changes that convention for the class, not for one key.

## Landing

Draft, and it stays draft: not enqueued, no auto-merge armed. `needs:contract-review` is on it because the claim comment declares `Clause-②: yes` — the accepted set does not grow, but the published declaration does, and this direction is a NARROWING of what an author may write.
